cls: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) - purine (dideoxyinosine) analog
quick: Weight-based: 400 mg once daily if >=60 kg, 250 mg once daily if <60 kg (delayed-release), on an empty stomach
Take on an empty stomach (>=30 min before or 2 h after food)
Avoid didanosine+stavudine combination (fatal lactic acidosis); use only if no alternative
Breastfeeding not recommended in HIV (and drug passes into milk)
Reduce dose by creatinine clearance; renally eliminated
Caution; risk of hepatic steatosis/lactic acidosis
Avoid - increases pancreatitis and hepatic risk
Amylase/lipase, signs of pancreatitis, neuropathy, lactate, LFTs, retinal exams in children
summary: Didanosine (ddI, dideoxyinosine) is a synthetic purine nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1 infection. It is largely superseded by safer agents. It carries a boxed warning for fatal and non-fatal pancreatitis and for lactic acidosis with severe hepatomegaly and steatosis (markedly increased when combined with stavudine, especially in pregnancy). It must be taken on an empty stomach and dosed by body weight and renal function.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents

dosage.d: 400 mg orally once daily on an empty stomach
dosage.n: Reduce to 250 mg once daily if co-administered with tenofovir

dosage.d: 250 mg orally once daily on an empty stomach
dosage.n: Reduce to 200 mg once daily if co-administered with tenofovir

dosage.d: Reduce dose according to creatinine clearance per product table
dosage.n: Renally eliminated; supplemental dosing considerations with dialysis

dosage.d: Per product-specific body-weight or body-surface-area regimen
dosage.t: Once or twice daily per formulation

admin: Take on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after eating
Swallow delayed-release capsules whole; do not open or crush
Stop the drug immediately and evaluate if pancreatitis is suspected
Avoid co-administration with stavudine; use caution and dose reduction with tenofovir
Separate from drugs whose absorption is pH-dependent (older buffered formulations)
moa: Didanosine is a synthetic analog of the purine nucleoside deoxyadenosine. After cellular uptake it is converted by host enzymes to its active metabolite dideoxyadenosine triphosphate (ddATP), which inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase both by competing with the natural substrate dATP and, after incorporation into viral DNA, by causing chain termination because it lacks the 3'-hydroxyl group needed for further nucleotide linkage. This blocks reverse transcription of the viral RNA genome.

absolute: Co-administration with allopurinol (markedly increases didanosine exposure)
Co-administration with ribavirin (fatal hepatic failure/pancreatitis/lactic acidosis)
relative: Combination with stavudine (especially in pregnancy) - fatal lactic acidosis
History of pancreatitis or risk factors for pancreatitis
Hepatic disease / risk factors for hepatic steatosis
Established or risk of non-cirrhotic portal hypertension
monitor: Serum amylase and lipase / signs of pancreatitis
Serum lactate and liver function (lactic acidosis/steatosis)
Signs of portal hypertension (esophageal varices, splenomegaly)

preg: Avoid if possible; the combination of didanosine with stavudine should NOT be used in pregnancy because of fatal lactic acidosis reported in pregnant women. If didanosine is unavoidable, use with close monitoring of lactate and hepatic function.
lact: Mothers with HIV are advised not to breastfeed to avoid postnatal transmission; in addition, didanosine may be excreted in breast milk.
renal: Didanosine is eliminated renally and accumulates in renal impairment - reduce the dose according to creatinine clearance using the product table, and account for hemodialysis.
hepatic: Use with caution; hepatic impairment increases the risk of hepatic steatosis and lactic acidosis. Monitor liver function and lactate, and stop if hepatotoxicity develops.

major: Allopurinol - greatly increases didanosine exposure; contraindicated
Ribavirin - fatal hepatic failure, pancreatitis, lactic acidosis; contraindicated
Stavudine - additive mitochondrial toxicity, fatal lactic acidosis; avoid
Tenofovir - raises didanosine levels and toxicity; reduce didanosine dose and monitor
Other drugs causing pancreatitis or peripheral neuropathy - additive toxicity
moderate: Methadone - reduces didanosine exposure (especially buffered forms)
Drugs needing gastric acid for absorption (e.g., ketoconazole, atazanavir) - separate dosing (buffered forms)
minor: Fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines (with old buffered formulations) - chelation; separate administration
interactions.food: Food substantially reduces absorption - take on an empty stomach (at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after eating).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it adds to the risk of pancreatitis and hepatic toxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes raised amylase/lipase, elevated lactate, raised liver enzymes and uric acid; may cause cytopenias.

common: Peripheral neuropathy (numbness, tingling, pain in feet/hands)
serious: Lactic acidosis with severe hepatomegaly and steatosis
Retinal changes and optic neuritis (especially in children)
emergency: Lactic acidosis (deep rapid breathing, severe fatigue, muscle pain)

monitoring: Serum amylase and lipase; clinical signs of pancreatitis
Peripheral neuropathy symptoms at each visit
Serum lactate and liver function (especially with risk factors)
Surveillance for portal hypertension/esophageal varices on long-term use
Periodic dilated retinal examination in children; HIV viral load and CD4 count
counsel: Take on an empty stomach - at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after food
Stop the drug and seek care urgently for severe stomach pain with vomiting (possible pancreatitis)
Report numbness, tingling or burning in the hands or feet (nerve effects)
Watch for unusual tiredness, fast breathing, muscle aches, or yellowing of skin/eyes (lactic acidosis/liver problems)
Avoid alcohol and do not take allopurinol or ribavirin with this medicine
pk: Antiviral activity over days to weeks as part of combination therapy
Plasma peak ~0.25-1.5 h (delayed-release reduces and delays peak)
Plasma ~1.5 h; intracellular ddATP half-life much longer (>12 h), allowing once-daily dosing
Long intracellular active-metabolite half-life supports once-daily regimens
Store at room temperature; protect from moisture; reconstituted pediatric solution refrigerated per label
pearls: Not currently FDA-active (largely withdrawn/superseded); content reflects the historical FDA/SmPC label and BNF - confirm against current local product information
BOXED WARNING: fatal and non-fatal PANCREATITIS, and LACTIC ACIDOSIS with severe hepatomegaly/steatosis (greatest risk with stavudine, especially in pregnancy)
Must be taken on an EMPTY STOMACH; food markedly lowers absorption
Contraindicated with allopurinol and with ribavirin; avoid with stavudine; reduce dose with tenofovir
Associated with non-cirrhotic portal hypertension on long-term use - a reason it is now seldom used
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day, on an empty stomach. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not take two doses at once. Maintaining adherence is important to keep HIV suppressed.
overdose: Experience is limited; expected effects relate to known toxicities - pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy, hyperuricemia, lactic acidosis and hepatic dysfunction. There is no specific antidote. Manage with supportive care; didanosine is partly removed by hemodialysis.
